It mainly carries out conventional hard X-ray absorption spectroscopy experiments, laser pump-X-ray probe time-resolved experiments, SAXS/WAXS/XAFS joint measurement experiments and XRD/XAFS joint measurement experiments. The line station provides continuously adjustable monochromatic X-ray from 5-18keV. Absorption spectroscopy experiments can be carried out in two modes: transmission and fluorescence. The fluorescence method uses Lytle detectors or self-developed array SDD systems. Time-resolved experiments can provide time-resolved XAFS experiments or XRD experiments of laser pump-X-ray probes, with a time resolution of up to 120 picoseconds. The joint measurement experiment can simultaneously collect the absorption spectrum, small-angle and wide-angle signals of the sample or the diffraction and absorption spectrum signals of the sample simultaneously. (Diffraction and wide-angle signal collection use a Mythen detector array with one-dimensional position resolution and no two-dimensional position resolution capability.)

The X-ray lithography station adjusts the light path through a reflector and can achieve hard line exposure (about 4.3keV) and soft line exposure (about 1.6keV) respectively. Hard line exposure uses synchrotron radiation white light to reach the sample through a beryllium window with a thickness of about 250um. It can achieve exposure of PMMA with a thickness exceeding 1.5mm and is mainly used in the development of microstructures with large aspect ratios. In soft line exposure, white light is reflected by a chromium mirror and then reaches the sample through a silicon nitride window with a thickness of about 0.5um. It can achieve photolithography of lines with a width of about 100 nanometers. It is mainly used in the development of sub-micron microstructures and mask preparation for hard line exposure.

It is mainly used for the preparation of X-ray optical components, especially for components containing large aspect ratio microstructures, such as X-ray refractive lenses, zone plates, gratings, etc. The achieved microstructure size and thickness cover a wide range, and its devices are widely used in the fields of X-ray focusing and imaging.

Main equipment of the experimental station
In addition to the exposure system of the synchrotron radiation lithography beam line, the lithography experimental station also has relatively complete micro-processing equipment and environment. The working environment includes a 300-square-meter thousand-level clean room, corrosion room, process auxiliary room, etc.; the equipment has a magnetron sputtering system, an atomic layer deposition system, a thermal evaporation system, an electroplating device, an oxidation furnace, a UV lithography machine, a reactive ion etching machine, an ion beam etching machine, and an ICP etching system; and testing equipment includes a step meter, a microscope, etc.

The X-ray lithography station (1B3A) of Beijing Synchrotron Radiation Facility is led by 1B3 bent iron. By adjusting the mirror system, two optical paths of reflected light and direct light can be realized, respectively, for nano-lithography suitable for sub-micron line width and X-ray depth lithography suitable for thickness greater than 1 mm. The reflector can move vertically to switch the light path. When the reflector moves away from the light path, the synchronization light enters the X-ray depth lithography exposure cavity; when the reflector cuts into the light path, the synchronization light enters the nanolithography exposure cavity after being reflected by the reflector, so the two exposure modes must be used in a time-sharing manner. The synchrotron radiation beam is uniformly distributed in the horizontal direction and Gaussian in the vertical direction. Therefore, the sample stage is scanned in the vertical direction to meet the large-area uniform spot required for photolithography. Figure 1 is a schematic structural diagram of the 1B3A photolithography beamline.

X-ray depth lithography
The 1B3A beam line is led from a bent iron, and the light source is illuminated on the sample through a beryllium window with a thickness of 250 microns. The spot size is approximately 55 mm horizontally and 10 mm vertically. The sample environment is a 50kpa helium atmosphere. The sample stage scans and exposes in the vertical direction. The maximum travel range is ±50 mm. Fixed-point exposure without scanning can also be achieved.
Wavelength range: White light, peak value approximately 4.3kev.
Exposure area: Maximum 50*80 mm.
Lithography Depth: Maximum lithography depth 1.5mm for PMMA photoresist.

nanolithography

The spot size is approximately 50 mm horizontally and 10 mm vertically. The sample environment is a vacuum, and the sample stage scans and exposes in the vertical direction, with a maximum travel range of ±50 mm. Fixed-point exposure without scanning can also be achieved.

Hard line exposure operation steps
(1) Turn on the cooling water. Open the plug button on the hard-wired water cooler and let the external circulation pump start. Turn on "POWER" on the water cooler panel and press the "COOL" button after about one minute.
(2) Place the sample. Fix the sample in the sample holder, insert the sample holder into the scanning frame in the hard-line exposure chamber, and tighten the screws to secure it. Close the exposure chamber door.
(3) Start scanning. On the touch screen hard-line exposure control system, set the "speed setting" and "swing setting" according to your own experimental needs. (Note that the parameters after "center height" cannot be changed.) After the settings are completed, click "Scan Start".
(4) Hutch door interlocking. Press the square green "Search" button inside the Hutch door, and the door warning light will flash and beep. Press the "Close" button outside the Hutch door and the door will automatically close. After the door is closed, click the square green "Search" button outside the door. After the beep ends, the round green light (Enable) under the safety gate on the safety interlock control system panel will light up.
(5) Vacuum. On the hard-wired control power box, press the "on" button of the mechanical pump, and the mechanical pump will start. Then press the "on" button of the front-stage valve, and you can hear a loud pumping sound, which will gradually become smaller. Evacuate to about 8Pa, press the "on" button of the foreline valve to close the foreline valve, and then press the "off" button of the mechanical pump.
(6) Fill with helium. Press the "Open" button of the helium filling valve and rotate the flow control valve on the helium bottle counterclockwise to fill the exposure chamber with helium. When the pressure reaches about 50KPa and the pressure difference is less than 1KPa, the helium filling valve will automatically close. Turn the flow control valve on the helium bottle clockwise to close.
(7) Open the gate valve. Press the "open" button of the gate valve to open the gate valve.
(8) Set exposure. On the LIGA light intensity acquisition software interface, enter the exposure amount in the box below "Target current value mAH", then click on the right-facing hollow arrow in the upper left corner, which changes to a solid arrow after clicking.
(9) Start exposure. Click the "Start" button on the LIGA light intensity acquisition interface, and then click the square "open/open" button under the safety gate on the BSRF safety interlock control system. You can hear the sound of the valve starting, and the warning lights on the FOE and Hutch light up. At this time, the exposure begins.
(10) Exposure ends. When the value under "Current and mAH" in the lower right corner of the LIGA light intensity collection interface is greater than or equal to the set exposure, the exposure will automatically stop. The square "open" button light under the safety shutoff on the BSRF safety interlock control system automatically goes out, and the red square "close" button below automatically lights up. The police lights on the FOE and Hutch automatically go off.
(11) Close the gate valve. Press the "open" button of the gate valve to close the gate valve.
(12) Stop scanning. Press the "stop button" on the touch screen to stop scanning, and then press the "return to origin" button, the scanning device will automatically return to the origin. After reaching the origin, the "Return to Origin" button will turn green and display "Return to Origin".
(13) Open the Hutch door. Press the "Open Door" button on the control box outside the door to open the Hutch door.
(14) Deflate. First, unscrew the fixing screw of the exposure chamber door and open the fixed door bolt. About half a minute after closing the gate valve, press the "open" button of the vent valve to deflate the exposure chamber. The sound of deflation can be heard during the deflation process.
(15) Take samples. After the deflation is completed, open the door of the hard-line exposure chamber, pull out the sample holder, and then close the door of the exposure chamber. Remove the sample from the sample holder.
(16) If you want to change the sample and continue the exposure, start the cycle from step (2). If you no longer want to continue to expose, press the "POWER" button of the water cooler to turn off the water cooler, and press the plug-in button on the water cooler to turn off the external circulation pump. Press the "ON" button of the mechanical pump, and then press the "ON" button of the foreline valve to evacuate the exposure chamber. After about 2 minutes, press the "on" button of the foreline valve, and then press the "off" button of the mechanical pump to turn off the mechanical pump.

After the beep ends, the round green light (Enable) under the safety gate on the safety interlock control system panel will light up.
(5) Turn on the mechanical pump. On the soft line control power supply box, press the "on" button of the mechanical pump, and the mechanical pump will start. Then press the "on" button of the front-end valve, and you can hear a loud pumping sound, which will gradually become smaller.
(6) Turn on the molecular pump. Evacuate to 14Pa, press the "on" button of the molecular pump, start the molecular pump, and press the "on" button of the ionizer switch.
(7) Open the pneumatic valve. When the vacuum is higher than 1.0X10-2Pa, press the "Open" button of pneumatic valve 1, then press the "Open" button of pneumatic valve 2, and open the two pneumatic valves in sequence.
(8) Set exposure. On the LIGA light intensity acquisition software interface, enter the exposure amount in the box below "Target current value mAH", then click on the right-facing hollow arrow in the upper left corner, which changes to a solid arrow after clicking.
(9) Start exposure. Click the "Start" button on the LIGA light intensity acquisition interface, and then click the square "open/open" button under the safety gate on the BSRF safety interlock control system. You can hear the sound of the valve starting, and the warning lights on the FOE and Hutch light up. At this time, the exposure begins.
(10) Exposure ends. When the value under "Current and mAH" in the lower right corner of the LIGA light intensity collection interface is greater than or equal to the set exposure, the exposure will automatically stop. The square "open" button light under the safety shutoff on the BSRF safety interlock control system automatically goes out, and the red square "close" button below automatically lights up. The police lights on the FOE and Hutch automatically go off.
(11) Close the pneumatic valve. Press the "Open" button of pneumatic valve 2, then press the "Open" button of pneumatic valve 1 to close both pneumatic valves in sequence.
(12) Stop scanning. Press the "stop button" on the touch screen to stop scanning, and then press the "return to origin" button, the scanning device will automatically return to the origin. After reaching the origin, the "Return to Origin" button will turn green and display "Return to Origin".
(13) Stop the molecular pump and mechanical pump. Press the "on" button of the power switch. Press the "ON" button of the molecular pump, and the molecular pump speed begins to decrease. When the molecular pump speed drops to 0, press the "ON" button of the foreline valve to close the foreline valve, and then press the "OFF" button of the mechanical pump to close the mechanical pump.
(14) Open the Hutch door. Press the "Open Door" button on the control box outside the door to open the Hutch door.
(15) Deflate. First, unscrew the fixing screw of the exposure chamber door and open the fixed door bolt. Press the "open" button of the deflation valve to deflate the exposure chamber. The sound of deflation can be heard during the deflation process.
(16) Take samples. After the deflation is completed, open the door of the cord exposure chamber, pull out the sample holder, and then close the door of the exposure chamber. Remove the sample from the sample holder.
(17) If you want to change the sample and continue the exposure, start the cycle from step (2). If you no longer want to continue to expose, press the "POWER" button of the water cooler to turn off the water cooler. Press the "ON" button of the mechanical pump, and then press the "ON" button of the foreline valve to evacuate the exposure chamber. After about 3 minutes, press the "on" button of the foreline valve, and then press the "off" button of the mechanical pump to turn off the mechanical pump.

The X-ray imaging experimental station is located at the end of the 4W1A beam line of the Beijing Synchrotron Radiation Facility. It is an experimental station for both white light and monochromatic light. In the more than ten years since the establishment of the 4W1A beamline and experimental station, it has been mainly used to analyze and study microstructural defects on the surface and inside of crystal materials and devices. After 2000, with the development of X-ray imaging technology, the beamline station became the base for domestic hard X-ray phase contrast imaging research, playing an increasingly important role in phase contrast imaging research in the fields of biology, medicine and materials. The experimental station has also built an X-ray nano-resolution three-dimensional imaging microscope. Using standard samples, the nanomicroscope can obtain spatial resolutions up to 30 nanometers (the spatial resolution obtained by actual samples varies with sample characteristics), which can provide advanced research methods for many disciplines such as life sciences, energy sciences, materials science, microelectronics industry, microprocessing technology and nanotechnology.

The main experimental methods carried out include crystal white light topography, micrometer resolution imaging and zone plate nanometer resolution full field imaging and corresponding CT experimental methods. In addition, the experimental station can also carry out research on phase contrast imaging methods, including diffraction enhanced imaging and coaxial phase contrast imaging.
Conduct analysis and research on microstructural defects on the surface and inside of crystal materials and devices.

light source
The light source of the 4W1A beam line is a single-period wiggler magnet, and the magnetic field strength of the light source magnet is 1.8T. Because the light source magnet is the first wiggler wiggler magnet in the 4th arc area of the electron storage ring, it is referred to as the 4W1 wiggler. When the electron beam passes through the magnetic field, it is subjected to the Lorentz force to produce circular acceleration motion, and synchrotron radiation X-rays are emitted from the tangential direction of the electron orbit. In the dedicated operation mode of synchrotron radiation (2.5GeV@250mA), the light source parameters of 4W1 (calculated based on coupling coefficient 10%) are:
Horizontal bundle size: sx=1.23mm
Bundle size in vertical direction: sy=0.42mm
Horizontal angular divergence: sx'=0.190mrad
Vertical angular divergence: sy'=0.131mrad

The main function of the dual-crystal monochromator is to monochromatize broad-spectrum white light X-rays into monochromatic X-rays of specific energy. It is the main optical component of the beam line experimental station. The dual-crystal monochromator consists of two perfect silicon single crystals and two sets of high-precision translation rotation stages. The diffraction surface of the silicon single crystal is Si(111), and the crystal plane spacing d111= 3.1353Å. The process of selecting monochromatic X-rays for a monochromator crystal is Bragg diffraction of the crystal diffraction face of X-rays. The relationship between the wavelength of monochromatic X-rays  and the The relationship between ray energy; the selection of monochromator energy can be automatically adjusted using micron resolution imaging control software.

The motion adjustment system of the experimental station is the key equipment to achieve fine adjustment of the main equipment of the experimental station, including the monochromator, sample stage and detector. It is built with KOHZU high-precision displacement stage and rotation stage. The sample stage adopts a five-dimensional adjustment mechanism, including rotation, horizontal and vertical adjustment of the sample stage, and two-dimensional adjustment of the sample rotation axis. The rotation and translation adjustment accuracy of the sample stage reaches ±0.005 degrees and ±0.3 microns respectively; the detector includes horizontal and vertical two-dimensional adjustments. Using stepper motors and controllers, the experimental station developed a motion adjustment system control program that can realize automatic adjustment of samples and efficient collection of CT data.

Through the double crystal monochromator of the experimental station, the white light X-rays at the beam line exit are monochromated, and monochromatic X-rays of a specific energy are selected to be irradiated on the sample. After absorption by the sample, a two-dimensional projection image of the internal microstructure of the sample is obtained on the detector. The optical path diagram of the micron resolution imaging experiment is shown in Figure 2. Due to the advantages of the 4W1 light source such as high brightness, high collimation, small luminous point size, and ultra-long object source distance, high-resolution images can be obtained. For example, a detector using a 10X lens can obtain a spatial resolution of approximately 1m. The experimental station has developed micron-resolution imaging data collection software based on the EPICS control system, which can realize a variety of imaging data collection functions, such as: single image collection, real-time collection; continuous collection with set intervals (suitable for in-situ experiments); CT collection of single energy points and flying CT collection based on external triggering. The software interface is shown in Figure 3.

The principle of X-ray nano-resolution three-dimensional imaging is shown in Figure 4. Through the zone plate "lens" magnification imaging, the CCD detector cooperates with the precision sample turntable to capture magnified projection images of the sample at different angles, and uses the CT reconstruction algorithm to obtain the three-dimensional density distribution of the sample. This X-ray microscope currently provides two experimental modes: high-resolution mode and large field of view mode: the high-resolution mode has an imaging field of view of 15 μm × 15 μm, and the achievable resolution is 50 nm (standard sample); the large field of view mode has an imaging field of view of 65 μm × 65 μm, and the achievable resolution is 150 nm (standard sample).

X-ray fluorescence spectrum analysis can be carried out, including conventional micro-area XRF, 2D\3D element distribution, X-ray emission spectroscopy (XES) and other experiments. Turning on the light refers to letting synchrotron radiation X-rays irradiate the sample. The steps to open the beam line are as follows:

1. Close the "safety shutter" (press the red button, the green button light goes out, and the red button light turns on)
2. Close the "No. 4 gate valve" (press the dark red button, the green indicator light of the valve goes out and the red indicator light turns on)

Based on the Arinax-MD2S diffractometer configured in this line station, this line station can provide a variety of crystal data collection strategies in addition to the traditional single-axis mode. For example:

In view of the difficulty in aligning the sample of microcrystals on the diffractometer and poor radiation resistance, the sample area is divided into grids with the same size as the light spot. A grid scanning method is used to quickly collect a diffraction pattern on each grid. The diffraction ability of each grid is obtained through preliminary processing and analysis of the diffraction pattern. Several grid points with strong diffraction ability are selected and 50 to 100 diffraction data are collected within a total rotation angle of 10 to 20 degrees. Then the diffraction data of multiple samples are automatically filtered and merged to obtain complete diffraction data.

If the crystal is larger than the beam size, the best practice to minimize radiation damage is to make the beam as large as the crystal. Spiral collection will help mitigate radiation damage by bringing a new volume of crystal into the beam for each image.

The data collection method of in situ flat plate protein crystals is a technology that directly collects X-ray diffraction data during the crystal growth process, avoiding the steps in traditional methods that require the crystals to be removed from the growth environment and frozen or transferred to other supports. This method is particularly suitable for studying the dynamic processes of protein crystals under natural growth conditions, such as crystal growth, phase transition or ligand binding.

The Pink Light Small Angle Scattering Station will provide users with experimental tests related to X-ray small angle scattering (SAXS). SAXS technology provides comprehensive structural information such as nanoscale particle size, shape, size distribution, periodicity, and fractal within the sample by measuring the scattering intensity distribution of X-rays in a small angle range after passing through the sample. Because SAXS technology adopts exposure-based acquisition, the acquisition time can be reduced to the order of milliseconds or even microseconds as the light flux increases. Therefore, it is suitable for dynamic changes in the structural characteristics of materials at the nanoscale, and is called an indispensable analysis tool in the fields of nanoscience, structural biology, and soft matter science. In addition, SAXS has a wide application range for samples and is simple to prepare. The sample state can be liquid, powder, film or even a mixture of them. SAXS tests are generally non-destructive and can be used repeatedly or for other measurements. In order to meet the regular testing needs of the majority of users, the Pink Light Small Angle Scattering System pursues the construction of a multi-functional SAXS line station with simple structure, high stability, high throughput, good statistics. Overview of the overall system design: a thin beam of fundamental wave radiation (8–12 keV) is generated by a vacuum external undulator with an energy bandwidth of 1.5% (this quasi-monochromatic light is called pink light). It is horizontally deflected and collimated and irradiated onto the sample. The scattered signals are received by the SAXS, WAXS and USAXS detectors placed in the optical path, respectively, to obtain scattered signals in different angle ranges.

As a dedicated coherent line station on HEPS, the hard X-ray coherent scattering station will make full use of the high brightness and high coherence of HEPS. It mainly includes two major types of coherent experimental methods, coherent X-ray diffraction imaging (CDI) and X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS).

For CDI, it specifically includes scanning coherence diffraction imaging (Ptychography), Bragg CDI (BCDI) and SAXS The three experimental technologies of CDI are mainly used for nanometer-resolution 3D structure imaging and strain imaging of samples. It can also be combined with X-ray fluorescence and absorption spectroscopy to achieve element imaging and valence state imaging. For example, it can be used for high-resolution 3D imaging of cells, providing the spatial arrangement relationship of various organelles in the cell and the fine structure of the organelles. It can be used to determine the 3D structure of metal glass shear bands, thereby providing the physical mechanism of plastic deformation and yielding. It can be used for various nanocrystal strains. For example, it helps to establish the relationship between catalytic activity and strain in catalysts, in-situ measurement of the defect distribution and movement of grains in lithium-ion battery cathode materials in battery materials, and measurement of the boundaries and defects of individual grains in polycrystalline materials. It can also be used to determine the structure of various micro-nano electronic devices such as integrated circuits. High-resolution 3D imaging of integrated circuits can help understand their functions, provide direct feedback on design and processing processes, quality control, and reverse engineering.

For XPCS, including small-angle and wide-angle modes, they can obtain the basic dynamic functions of the system, such as intermediate scattering functions and dynamic structure factors, etc., which are mainly used for the measurement of equilibrium dynamics, non-equilibrium dynamics and dynamic heterogeneity of condensed matter; for example, XPCS can be used to study the relaxation dynamics of various glass systems and colloidal systems. During the glass transition process, XPCS can completely measure α relaxation and β relaxation in glass transition, which helps to improve the understanding of glass transition and the nature of glass; it can be used to measure the fluctuations of various order parameters in strongly correlated electronic systems, including charge order, spin order, magnetic domain, etc.; it can also be used to measure surface interface dynamics, such as diffusion behavior, self-assembly behavior and kinetic transitions at the nanoparticle emulsion interface.

The X-ray absorption spectroscopy line station is a high-performance hard X-ray beamline led by an insert and optimized for X-ray absorption spectroscopy and related derivative experimental methods. The basic goal of the design is to have strong versatility, large energy coverage, and a high-throughput, high-brightness XAFS experimental system to provide users with a reliable, stable, and easy-to-operate absorption spectroscopy experimental platform. The platform has conventional experimental methods for X-ray absorption spectroscopy, has time resolution and spatial resolution capabilities, and can detect micro-area/surface/interface structures. At the same time, the online station also provides users with a variety of in-situ sample environments, and combined with experimental methods such as XRF/XRD/FTIR/mass spectrometry, it can provide richer sample information. At the same time, the design provides the possibility for the development of other experimental methods and new experimental methods. The target energy covers 4.8–45 keV (covering the K-edge XAFS energy range of element 22, Ti-60, Nd, and covering the L-edge of element 55, Cs and above).

Stable and efficient absorption spectrum testing in the X-ray energy range of 2.1 keV ~ 10 keV to obtain information including the chemical form, geometric structure and electronic structure of substances.

Covering X-rays in the medium energy range, it can develop the K absorption edge of low Z elements (S, P, Cl, Ar, K, Ca) and heavy metal elements (Cu, Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, etc.), as well as the L and M absorption edges of transition metal elements; the sample forms are diverse (solid, liquid, gas, mixed state); the sample environment is diverse: in-situ electrochemistry, electrocatalysis, high and low temperature, etc.
The experimental station consists of two parts: the vacuum chamber and the EXAFS device.

The vacuum degree can reach below 1E-4 Pa. It is generally used for absorption edge testing of elements in the low energy range of 2.1-5.0 keV. The modes include the total electron yield method (TEY) and the partial fluorescence method (PFY). Vacuum and helium atmospheres can be converted into each other to reduce air absorption. Liquid samples of low-energy elements can be tested in a helium atmosphere.

In the atmospheric environment, it is generally used for absorption edge testing of elements higher than 5 keV. Transmission method (TM) and fluorescence yield method (PFY) can be used; it has three ionization chambers, and the test sample is placed between the front ionization chamber 1 and the rear ionization chamber 2. A standard filter disk is placed in front of the rear ionization chamber 3 to calibrate the energy in real time.

The EXAFS device is equipped with a 6-axis sampling manipulator and sample tray, which can accommodate 50 samples at the same time, and the sample change time is <10 seconds; the control system is embedded in the spectrum acquisition program, which can automatically replace samples and continuously collect spectra without manual intervention.

A KB focusing mirror is installed behind the experimental station to focus the light spot to about 13 µm × 14 µm, with a working distance of about 200 mm, which is suitable for small focus spot experimental tests.

It is used for solid samples in the atmospheric environment. It can be heated from room temperature to 873 K with an accuracy of ±1°C. The temperature can be controlled locally or remotely. It is compatible with transmission and fluorescence modes. A gas circulation device is installed on the top to pass in reaction gases to achieve in-situ solid-gas phase reaction. A sapphire window installed on the same side of the sample surface can introduce external trigger light to achieve photocatalytic reaction conditions.

Liquid nitrogen refrigeration, temperature control range 80–300 K (room temperature), liquid nitrogen capacity 1.6 L; target temperature can be reached in 30 minutes at the fastest, temperature control stability ±0.1 K; equipped with two sample rods (can hold 2 samples each time), easy to replace in about 5 minutes; good sealing, stable at low temperatures for more than 10 hours; inner window diameter 15 mm (120 µm high-purity Be film window), outer window diameter 35 mm (120 µm Mylar window); equipped with fluorescence and transmission sample holders.

Two 7-yuan SDD detectors are located in the vacuum chamber and the EXAFS device respectively; equipped with a large-area fluorescence detector suitable for fluorescence signal collection of low-concentration samples.

The self-developed absorption spectroscopy data acquisition system enables free switching of dual acquisition spectroscopy systems; it is embedded with functions such as automatic gas distribution and automatic sample change, making it user-friendly.

Two sets of absorption spectrum data analysis software developed by HEPS Computing and Network Communication System support real-time online or offline processing of XAS match, PCA‑LCF and extended edge fitting.

All-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSB) have the potential of high specific energy, high safety and low cost. Pang Quanquan's research group at Peking University designed a composite solid-state sulfur cathode to trigger a rapid sulfur solidification reaction, allowing the battery to exhibit excellent fast-charging performance. The K-edge XANES of S was used to test the valence state evolution of the sulfur cathode during the charge and discharge process: S in the original electrode was converted into Li2S and Li2Sx after the first discharge; after full charge, Li2S and Li2Sx were completely converted into sulfur; after another discharge, the sulfur was converted into Li2S and Li2Sx, showing good reversibility. Relevant results were published in Nature (2025), DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08298-9.

The concentration and isotopic characteristics of Hg2+ and Hg0 in the peat soil at different depths in the peatland system in northern Sweden were studied to reveal the redox transformation process of mercury after deposition: dry and wet sedimentation inputs 36% of mercury into peatlands, and peat vegetation absorbs 64%; surface photochemical reduction causes about 30% of Hg2+ to be reduced to Hg0 and released to the atmosphere every year; dark oxidation of organic matter above the water table reduces Hg0 Concentration; supersaturated Hg0 below water table More from direct photochemical reduction of Hg2+ in rainwater. Related research used the BSRF 4B7A line station for sulfur speciation analysis and was published in Nature Communications (2023) 14:7389.
